trust_decision.summary: Whether an unauthenticated POST /api/v1alpha1/autobuild is from a real git provider is decided by header-based provider detection in the handler, the per-provider secret load in the autobuild service and the provider's ValidateWebhookPayload; with an X-Event-Key header the Bitbucket path skips validation (no signature header, empty secret allowed, empty token accepted), and nothing ties the detected provider to the host of the component's repo, so any caller can trigger builds for any auto-build component.

landing_point.why: The summary says webhook signature bypass via git-provider confusion; the Bitbucket validator returns nil on an empty token and carries a TODO for HMAC, so it is the obvious first stop.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /api/v1alpha1/autobuild (X-Hub-Signature-256) -> GitHubProvider.ValidateWebhookPayload; refactored onto new shared verifyHMACSHA256 (fix.diff:1670-1712), which adds a fail-closed empty-secret check
POST /api/v1alpha1/autobuild -> detectGitProviderFromParams (Bitbucket signature header was empty)
POST /api/v1alpha1/autobuild -> autobuildService.ProcessWebhook (allowEmpty derived from empty signature header)
POST /api/v1alpha1/autobuild -> getWebhookSecret (missing/empty key accepted when allowEmpty)
POST /api/v1alpha1/autobuild -> webhookProcessor.findAffectedComponents (no provider-vs-repo-host consistency check; fix adds providerFromRepoURL, fix.diff:1352-1395)
OpenAPI contract for POST /api/v1alpha1/autobuild (adds X-Hub-Signature header param)
generated ServerInterfaceWrapper.HandleAutoBuild header binding (plus models.gen.go:4125 HandleAutoBuildParams, client.gen.go:11209)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: internal/openchoreo-api/services/autobuild/service.go:56-57 and :93-108 (allowEmpty default makes a missing/empty secret valid); second out-of-scope site internal/openchoreo-api/services/autobuild/webhook_processor.go:139-146 (component matching has no provider/host binding)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Once Bitbucket HMAC is enforced in bitbucket.go, the secret loader's allowEmpty path and the component matcher look like unrelated plumbing / repo-matching logic, and self-hosted hosts cannot be mapped to a provider anyway, so a provider-consistency check looks like a feature, not a security fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Signed Bitbucket and GitHub webhooks must still trigger builds; components on self-hosted hosts (unknown provider) must still match without a provider check; a repo path containing another provider's domain (bitbucket.org/org/github.com-sync) must not be misclassified; SSH/.git/case URL variants must still match. Rejecting all Bitbucket, or requiring a provider match for unknown hosts, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: Bitbucket request with no signature header
Bitbucket request with signature but no/empty bitbucket-secret key configured
signature without sha256= prefix / wrong digest
empty configured secret for GitHub (new fail-closed check in verifyHMACSHA256)
provider confusion: one provider's headers with a payload naming a repo hosted on another provider
repo URL shapes: https, git@host:path, ssh://, .git suffix, subdomains (*.github.com), other provider domain in path

O7_producer.where: internal/openchoreo-api/services/autobuild/service.go:83-108 (getWebhookSecret), driven by the handler's signature-header choice at internal/openchoreo-api/api/handlers/webhook_handler.go:59

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GitLab token check compares X-Gitlab-Token to the secret with plain != (not constant time) and was not moved onto the shared verifier
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: GitLab already requires a non-empty token and secret; timing comparison is a different weakness from the advisory's bypass.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a GitLab variant that skips validation when the configured secret is empty, mirroring the Bitbucket allowEmpty behaviour
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same allowEmpty plumbing exists in service.go; a maintainer could have made secrets optional for 'unsigned GitLab hooks' during development.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an additional provider (e.g. Gitea/Bitbucket Server via X-Gitea-Event or X-Request-UUID) detected by an event header and returning an empty signature header
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The detection switch is header-driven and extensible; adding a provider by event-header only is exactly how the Bitbucket case was written.

O9_family: authentication bypass / missing webhook signature verification (CWE-287/290/345)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.24.12 (go.mod:3); oapi-codegen needed only if the solver regenerates gen/*.gen.go from openapi
O10_build.project_tests: go test ./internal/openchoreo-api/services/autobuild/... ./internal/openchoreo-api/api/handlers/... using controller-runtime fake client (internal/openchoreo-api/services/autobuild/webhook_processor_test.go:547); no tests in services/git at pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Make BitbucketProvider.ValidateWebhookPayload reject an empty token (or add HMAC there) without wiring the X-Hub-Signature header, removing allowEmpty, or binding the provider to the component's repo host.

out_of_scope_notes: TriggerWorkflow is also reached by authenticated API/MCP paths (internal/openchoreo-api/services/workflowrun/service_authz.go:164), guarded by authz, not webhook signatures; not pursued.
Provider-consistency check in the fix deliberately does nothing for self-hosted hosts (fix.diff:1356-1357).
